content:
Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman today gave a detailed account of the future direction of the Apple Watch product line.

He pointed out that, facing fierce competition from the Oura Ring and other screenless smart fitness devices, Apple is rethinking the positioning of the Apple Watch from scratch. It seems Apple is preparing to completely revolutionise the concept of the Apple Watch from the ground up……

Although the plans do not yet appear to be finalised, Apple is considering various shapes and sizes, including watches with circular faces, as well as fitness accessories with no screen at all. This would represent a major shift in the history of the Apple Watch, since every model so far has essentially followed the same basic design concept.

Bloomberg noted that Apple is exploring possibilities for both the entry-level and high-end markets, weighing the appeal of launching more premium and more affordable models. These new wearable form factors will also tie in with software changes, with Apple planning to push its health applications towards an AI-centric direction.

However, nothing is anywhere near production yet. From the sound of it, Apple does not even seem to have settled on a concrete plan so far. So any fundamentally new design is still several years away from hitting the market.

This autumn, Apple will launch new iterative models, including the Apple Watch Series 12 and the Ultra 4. The new watches will come with a new CPU, a few new colour options, and enhanced fitness features.

The new Apple Watch is likely to make its debut at the company's annual September event, which will also see the unveiling of the all-new iPhone 18 Pro and the first foldable iPhone, the latter possibly named the "iPhone Ultra".
